statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the connection is established, the NNTP server host MUST send a greeting.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client host and server host then exchange commands and responses (respectively) until the connection is closed or aborted.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: ...until the connection is closed or aborted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The further data may be sent... following a request from the server (indicated by a 3xx response).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the connection is established, the NNTP server host MUST send a greeting.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The further data may be sent... following a request from the server (indicated by a 3xx response).
actions: server requests further data from client

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The client host and server host then exchange commands and responses (respectively) until the connection is closed or aborted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the timer expires, the server SHOULD close the connection without sending any response to the client.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The receipt of any command from the client during the timer interval SHOULD suffice to reset the autologout timer.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The receipt of any significant amount of data from a client that is sending a multi-line data block (such as during a POST or IHAVE command) SHOULD suffice to reset the autologout timer.
statements.trigger: significant data received from client in multi-line block

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In a multi-line response, the block immediately follows the CRLF at the end of the initial line of the response.
statements.trigger: CRLF at end of initial response line

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The lines of the block MUST be followed by a terminating line consisting of a single termination octet followed by a CRLF pair. The terminating line MUST NOT be considered part of the multi-line block.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A multi-line data block is used in certain commands and responses, consisting of a sequence of zero or more lines followed by a terminating line.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 2xx - Command completed OK

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 3xx - Command OK so far; send the rest of it
actions: send remainder of command to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 4xx - Command was syntactically correct but failed for some reason

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 5xx - Command unknown, unsupported, unavailable, or syntax error
actions: treat command as unknown or unsupported

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client receives an unexpected response, it SHOULD use the first digit of the response to determine the result. For example, an unexpected 2xx should be taken as success, and an unexpected 4xx or 5xx as failure.
actions: evaluate response.code[0] to determine success or failure

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each response MUST begin with a three-digit status indicator.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST respond to any command with the appropriate generic response (given in Section 3.2.1) if it represents the situation. Otherwise, each recognized command MUST return one of the response codes specifically listed in its description or in an extension.
actions: send appropriate generic response or command-specific response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server has to terminate the connection for some reason, it MUST give a 400 response code to the next command and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 502: It is necessary to terminate the connection and to start a new one with the appropriate authority before the command can be used. The server MUST NOT close the connection immediately after a 502 response except at the initial connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 502: It is necessary to terminate the connection and to start a new one with the appropriate authority before the command can be used. Server MUST NOT close the connection immediately after a 502 response (except at initial connection).
actions: client starts new connection with appropriate authority

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 480: The client must authenticate itself to the server before the facility can be used on this connection. This will involve the use of an authentication extension.
actions: client must authenticate via authentication extension

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 483: The client must negotiate appropriate privacy protection on the connection. This will involve the use of a privacy extension such as [NNTP-TLS].

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 401: The client must change the state of the connection in some other manner. The first argument of the response MUST be the capability label of the facility that provides the necessary mechanism.
actions: client changes connection state via named capability

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the server has to terminate the connection for some reason, it MUST give a 400 response code to the next command and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 401: The first argument of the response MUST be the capability label (see Section 5.2) of the facility that provides the necessary mechanism.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: [Server closes connection.] — example of the server needing to close down immediately after sending a 400 response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of the server needing to close down immediately: [C] ARTICLE 123 [S] 400 Power supply failed, running on UPS [Server closes connection.]

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to access a facility not available to this connection: [C] MODE READER [S] 200 Reader mode, posting permitted

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In reader mode, IHAVE is not available: [C] IHAVE <i.am.an.article.you.will.want@example.com> [S] 500 Permission denied

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to access a facility requiring authentication: [C] GROUP secret.group [S] 480 Permission denied

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of a successful attempt following authentication: [C] XSECRET fred flintstone [S] 290 Password for fred accepted [C] GROUP secret.group [S] 211 5 1 20 secret.group selected

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to access a facility requiring privacy: [C] GROUP secret.group [S] 483 Secure connection required

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example: [C] XENCRYPT [Client and server negotiate encryption on the link] [S] 283 Encrypted link established

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of a need to change mode before a facility is used: [C] GROUP binary.group [S] 401 XHOST Not on this virtual host

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example: [C] XHOST binary.news.example.org [S] 290 binary.news.example.org virtual host selected; subsequently [C] GROUP binary.group [S] 211 5 1 77 binary.group selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST ensure that the capability list accurately reflects the capabilities (including extensions) currently available. If a capability is only available with the server in a certain state (for example, only after authentication), the list MUST only include the capability label when the server is in that state.
statements.guard_semantics: server.capability_list = f(server.state)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, if only some of the commands in an extension will be available, or if the behaviour of the extension will change in some other manner, according to the state of the server, this MUST be indicated by different arguments in the capability line.
statements.guard_semantics: capability_line.arguments = f(server.state)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Where a server does not implement a command, it MUST always generate a 500 generic response code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A 501 generic response code in the case of a variant of a command depending on a second keyword where the base command is recognised.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Some commands have cases that require other commands to be used first. If the former command is implemented but the latter is not, the former MUST still generate the relevant specific response code. For example, if ARTICLE is implemented but GROUP is not, the correct response to 'ARTICLE 1234' remains 412.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the capability label is included in the capability list returned by the server, the server MUST support all commands in that bundle.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The second use is for the bulk transfer of articles from one store to another... this process is called 'peering' or 'transit'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The first use is 'reading', where the client fetches articles from a large store maintained by the server for immediate or later presentation to a user.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY provide different modes of behaviour (transit, reader, or a combination) to different client connections.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Except as an effect of the MODE READER command (Section 5.3) on a mode-switching server, once a server advertises either or both of the IHAVE or READER capabilities, it MUST continue to advertise them for the entire session.
actions: server changes advertised capabilities per MODE READER effect

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once a server advertises either or both of the IHAVE or READER capabilities, it MUST continue to advertise them for the entire session.
statements.guard_semantics: Once set to IHAVE or READER (or both), must remain set for session duration unless MODE READER command is issued on a mode-switching server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Transit mode, which applies after the initial connection. It MUST advertise the MODE-READER capability. It MUST NOT advertise the READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Reading mode, after a successful MODE READER command. It MUST NOT advertise the MODE-READER capability. It MUST advertise the READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Reading mode is entered after a successful MODE READER command.
statements.post_cond: server.mode = Reading mode & server.advertises_MODE_READER = false & server.advertises_READER = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In Transit mode, the server MAY cease to advertise the MODE-READER capability after the client uses any command except CAPABILITIES.
statements.guard_semantics: server.mode = Transit mode & client.last_command != CAPABILITIES

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In Reading mode, the server MAY NOT advertise the IHAVE capability, even if it was advertising it in transit mode.
statements.guard_semantics: server.mode = Reading mode

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD only issue a MODE READER command to a server if it is advertising the MODE-READER capability. If the client wishes to use any reader commands, it SHOULD use the MODE READER command immediately after the initial connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The initial connection must not be part of a pipeline; that is, the client MUST NOT send any command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the greeting.
statements.trigger: receive CRLF at end of greeting

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the specific description of a command says it 'MUST NOT be pipelined', that command MUST end any pipeline of commands. That is, the client MUST NOT send any following command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the response from the command.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT send any following command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the response from the [MUST NOT be pipelined] command.
statements.trigger: receive CRLF at end of response

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The initial connection must not be part of a pipeline; the client MUST NOT send any command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the greeting.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Except where stated otherwise, a client MAY use pipelining. That is, it may send a command before receiving the response for the previous command.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the specific description of a command says it 'MUST NOT be pipelined', the client MUST NOT send any following command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the response from the command.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the specific description of a command says it 'MUST NOT be pipelined', that command MUST end any pipeline of commands.
statements.guard_semantics: When true, client must not send subsequent command until CRLF of response is received

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: These are the only valid response codes for the initial greeting; the server MUST not return any other generic response code.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 200 Service available, posting allowed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 201 Service available, posting prohibited

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Following a 400 or 502 response, the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These are the only valid response codes for the initial greeting; the server MUST not return any other generic response code.
statements.guard_semantics: protocol.state = Initial Greeting

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 200 Service available, posting allowed — initial greeting response transitions session to posting-allowed state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 201 Service available, posting prohibited — initial greeting response transitions session to posting-prohibited state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 400 Service temporarily unavailable. Following a 400 response, the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 502 Service permanently unavailable. Following a 502 response, the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: There is no command presented by the client upon initial connection to the server. The server MUST present an appropriate response code as a greeting to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client including POST, the server MUST present a 200 greeting code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client, but the client is not authorized to post articles using the POST command, the server MUST present a 201 greeting code.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Otherwise, the server MUST present a 400 or 502 greeting code and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client including POST, the server MUST present a 200 greeting code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client, but the client is not authorized to post articles using the POST command, the server MUST present a 201 greeting code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 400 SHOULD be used if the issue is only temporary (for example, because of load) and the client can expect to be able to connect successfully at some point in the future without making any changes. The server MUST present a 400 greeting code and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 502 MUST be used if the client is not permitted under any circumstances to interact with the server, and MAY be used if the server has insufficient information to determine whether the issue is temporary or permanent. The server MUST present a 502 greeting code and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: [Initial connection set-up completed.]

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 200 NNTP Service Ready, posting permitted

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 201 NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: [Server closes connection.]

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Example of a normal connection from an authorized client that then terminates the session: [Initial connection set-up completed.] [S] 200 NNTP Service Ready, posting permitted
statements.post_cond: session.state = NNTP Service Ready, posting permitted
actions: server sends 200 NNTP Service Ready, posting permitted

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Example of a normal connection from an authorized client that is not permitted to post: [Initial connection set-up completed.] [S] 201 NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited
statements.post_cond: session.state = NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited
actions: server sends 201 NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Example of a normal connection from an unauthorized client: [Initial connection set-up completed.] [S] 502 NNTP Service permanently unavailable [Server closes connection.]
actions: server sends 502 NNTP Service permanently unavailable

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Example of a connection from a client if the server is unable to provide service: [Initial connection set-up completed.] [S] 400 NNTP Service temporarily unavailable [Server closes connection.]
actions: server sends 400 NNTP Service temporarily unavailable

statements.subject: session
statements.description: [C] QUIT [S] 205 NNTP Service exits normally [Server closes connection.] — from posting permitted state
actions: server sends 205 NNTP Service exits normally

statements.subject: session
statements.description: [C] QUIT [S] 205 NNTP Service exits normally [Server closes connection.] — from posting prohibited state
actions: server sends 205 NNTP Service exits normally

statements.subject: server
statements.description: CAPABILITIES command: Responses: 101 Capability list follows (multi-line)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command MAY be issued at any time; the server MUST NOT require it to be issued in order to make use of any capability.
actions: send capability list as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not recognise the argument (and it is a keyword), it MUST respond with the 101 response code as if the argument had been omitted.
statements.trigger: CAPABILITIES command received with unrecognized keyword argument
actions: send capability list as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an argument is provided that the server does recognise, it MAY use the 101 response code or MAY use some other response code.
statements.trigger: CAPABILITIES command received with recognized argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is not a keyword, the 501 generic response code MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: CAPABILITIES command received with non-keyword argument

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The response generated by this command MAY change during a session because of other state information (which, in turn, may be changed by the effects of other commands or by external events).
statements.guard_semantics: capability_list reflects current session state and external events at time of command issuance

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 200 Posting allowed — state entered after a successful MODE READER command where posting is permitted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 201 Posting prohibited — state entered after a successful MODE READER command where posting is not permitted.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Following a 502 response the server MUST immediately close the connection — terminal state after reading service is permanently unavailable.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: MODE READER command yields 200; session transitions to Posting Allowed state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: MODE READER command yields 201; session transitions to Posting Prohibited state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Following a 502 response the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command MUST NOT be pipelined.
statements.guard_semantics: MODE READER must not be sent while another command is outstanding in the pipeline

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server is mode-switching, it switches from its transit mode to its reader mode

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server is mode-switching, it switches from its transit mode to its reader mode

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server is mode-switching, it switches from its transit mode to its reader mode, indicating this by changing the capability list accordingly. It MUST then return a 200 or 201 response with the same meaning as for the initial greeting.
actions: change capability list to reader mode

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the MODE READER command is issued, the server MAY reset its state to that immediately after the initial connection before switching mode.
actions: reset state to immediately after initial connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it advertises the READER capability, it MUST return a 200 or 201 response with the same meaning as for the initial greeting; in this case, the command MUST NOT affect the server state in any way.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it does not advertise the READER capability, it MUST return a 502 response and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT issue MODE READER more than once in a session or after any security or privacy commands are issued.
statements.guard_semantics: session.mode_reader_issued = false & session.security_or_privacy_command_issued = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MODE READER command on a transit-only server: server responds '502 Transit service only' and closes connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MODE READER command on a server that provides reading facilities: server responds '200 Reader mode, posting permitted'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MODE READER command on a mode-switching server: server transitions from transit mode to reader mode and responds '200 Reader mode, posting permitted'; capabilities change accordingly.
statements.post_cond: session.mode = reader & session.posting = permitted & server.capability = READER
actions: switch advertised capabilities to reader mode set

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MODE READER command where the client is not permitted to post: server responds '201 NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited'.
actions: send 201 NNTP Service Ready, posting prohibited

statements.subject: server
statements.description: IHAVE command issued in reader mode: server responds '500 Permission denied'; session remains in reader mode.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Reader mode, posting permitted: the session state entered after a successful MODE READER where the client is allowed to post.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Reader mode, posting prohibited: the session state entered after a successful MODE READER where the client is not permitted to post (201 response).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Response 205: Connection closing

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: QUIT command causes the connection to begin closing; server responds with 205 Connection closing.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client uses the QUIT command to terminate the session. The server MUST acknowledge the QUIT command and then close the connection to the client.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client uses the QUIT command to terminate the session. The server MUST acknowledge the QUIT command and then close the connection to the client. Server responds 205.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The server MUST NOT generate any response code to the QUIT command other than 205 or, if any arguments are provided, 501.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a client simply disconnects (or if the connection times out or some other fault occurs), the server MUST gracefully cease its attempts to service the client, disconnecting from its end if necessary.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client sends QUIT; server responds with 205 closing connection; server closes connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: At the start of an NNTP session, the 'currently selected newsgroup' value is set to the special value 'invalid'.
statements.guard_semantics: initialized to 'invalid' at session start

statements.subject: session
statements.description: At the start of an NNTP session, the 'current article number' value is set to the special value 'invalid'.
statements.guard_semantics: initialized to 'invalid' at session start

statements.subject: session
statements.description: At the start of an NNTP session, both 'currently selected newsgroup' and 'current article number' are set to the special value 'invalid'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: GROUP group command; response 211 number low high group — Group successfully selected
actions: send 211 response with number, low, high, group

statements.subject: server
statements.description: GROUP group command; response 411 — No such newsgroup
statements.trigger: GROUP command received with nonexistent newsgroup

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Indicating capability: READER — GROUP command requires READER capability

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The GROUP or LISTGROUP command MUST be used by a client, and a successful response received, before any other command is used that depends on the value of the currently selected newsgroup or current article number. This implies a session state in which no newsgroup is currently selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a valid group is selected by means of the GROUP command, the currently selected newsgroup MUST be set to that group, and the current article number MUST be set to the first article in the group.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a valid group is selected by means of this command, the currently selected newsgroup MUST be set to that group. If an invalid group is specified, the currently selected newsgroup MUST NOT be changed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a valid group is selected by means of this command, the current article number MUST be set to the first article in the group. If an empty newsgroup is selected, the current article number is made invalid. If an invalid group is specified, the current article number MUST NOT be changed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a valid non-empty group is selected by means of the GROUP command, the currently selected newsgroup MUST be set to that group, and the current article number MUST be set to the first article in the group (this applies even if the group is already the currently selected newsgroup).
actions: set currently selected newsgroup to requested group
set current article number to first article in group
return 211 response with article count and water marks

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If an empty newsgroup is selected, the currently selected newsgroup MUST be set to that group, and the current article number is made invalid.
actions: set currently selected newsgroup to requested group

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If an invalid group is specified, the currently selected newsgroup and current article number MUST NOT be changed. If the group specified is not available on the server, a 411 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: GROUP command (group not available on server)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LISTGROUP with a valid group (or with a group already selected) returns 211 with article numbers (multi-line).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LISTGROUP with a group name that does not exist returns 411 No such newsgroup.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LISTGROUP with no group specified and no newsgroup currently selected returns 412 No newsgroup selected. The 412 response can only occur if no group has been specified.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The 412 response can only occur if no group has been specified (in the LISTGROUP command).
statements.guard_semantics: 412 response is only possible when the group parameter is absent from the command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The LISTGROUP command selects a newsgroup in the same manner as the GROUP command; on success a 211 response is returned and the command sets the current article number to the first article in the group, if any.
statements.trigger: LISTGROUP command with valid available group argument
actions: set current article number to first article in group

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the group specified is not available on the server, a 411 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: LISTGROUP command with unavailable group argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no group is specified and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: LISTGROUP command with no group argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no group is specified, the currently selected newsgroup is used; on success the command sets the current article number to the first article in the group, if any.
statements.trigger: LISTGROUP command with no group argument and valid current group
actions: set current article number to first article in group

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The currently selected newsgroup can be valid or invalid; if no group is specified and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned.
statements.guard_semantics: Determines whether LISTGROUP without argument succeeds (211) or fails (412)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When successful, the LISTGROUP command sets the current article number to the first article in the group, if any, even if this is not within the range specified by the second argument.
statements.guard_semantics: Set to first article in group on successful LISTGROUP, regardless of range argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LAST command: response 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LAST command: response 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LAST command: response 422 No previous article in this group
statements.pre_cond: session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_number_valid = true & session.previous_article_exists = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LAST command: response 223 Article found; article pointer moved to previous article
statements.pre_cond: session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_number_valid = true & session.previous_article_exists = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: LAST command requires READER capability; a newsgroup must be selected and the current article number must be valid for the command to succeed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the currently selected newsgroup is valid, the current article number MUST be set to the previous article in that newsgroup (the highest existing article number less than the current article number). If successful, a response indicating the new current article number and the message-id of that article MUST be returned.
statements.pre_cond: session.newsgroup_valid = true & session.article_number_valid = true & session.article_number > session.low_water_mark
actions: set current article number to highest existing article number less than current
return success response with new article number and message-id

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the current article number is already the first article of the newsgroup, a 422 response MUST be returned. The currently selected newsgroup and current article number MUST NOT be altered.
actions: leave newsgroup and article number unchanged

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the current article number is invalid, a 420 response MUST be returned. The currently selected newsgroup and current article number MUST NOT be altered.
actions: leave newsgroup and article number unchanged

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned. The currently selected newsgroup and current article number MUST NOT be altered.
actions: leave newsgroup and article number unchanged

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful article retrieval using LAST: LAST command issued and a previous article exists; server responds 223 and moves current article pointer to the previous article.
actions: send 223 response with previous article number and message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article without having selected a group (via the GROUP command) first: currently selected newsgroup is invalid; server responds 412 no newsgroup selected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article using the LAST command when the current article number is that of the first article in the group: server responds 422 No previous article to retrieve.
actions: send 422 No previous article to retrieve

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article using the LAST command when the currently selected newsgroup is empty: server responds 420 No current article selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NEXT command response 412: No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NEXT command response 420: Current article number is invalid
actions: send 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NEXT command response 421: No next article in this group
statements.pre_cond: session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_valid = true & session.next_article_exists = false
actions: send 421 No next article in this group

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NEXT command response 223 n message-id: Article found
statements.pre_cond: session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_valid = true & session.next_article_exists = true
actions: advance current article pointer to next article

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NEXT requires the READER capability to be indicated

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the currently selected newsgroup is valid, the current article number MUST be set to the next article in that newsgroup (that is, the lowest existing article number greater than the current article number). If successful, a response indicating the new current article number and the message-id of that article MUST be returned.
actions: set current article number to lowest existing article number greater than current
return success response with new current article number and message-id

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the current article number is already the last article of the newsgroup, a 421 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: NEXT command received when current article is last article

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the currently selected newsgroup is valid, the current article number MUST be set to the next article in that newsgroup.
statements.guard_semantics: session.newsgroup_selected = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of a successful article retrieval using NEXT: GROUP is selected, NEXT advances to the next article and server responds 223 with new article number and message-id.
actions: send 223 response with new current article number and message-id

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article without having selected a group first: currently selected newsgroup is invalid, NEXT returns 412 no newsgroup selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article using NEXT when the current article number is that of the last article in the group: server responds 421 No next article to retrieve.
actions: send 421 No next article to retrieve

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve an article using NEXT when the currently selected newsgroup is empty: server responds 420 No current article selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Assumes currently selected newsgroup is invalid — the session is in a state where no valid newsgroup has been selected, causing NEXT to return 412.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): ARTICLE message-id -> 220 0|n message-id Article follows (multi-line)
actions: send 220 response with article-id and multi-line article body

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): ARTICLE message-id -> 430 No article with that message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): ARTICLE number -> 220 n message-id Article follows (multi-line)
actions: send 220 response with article number, message-id, and multi-line article body

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): ARTICLE number -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): ARTICLE number -> 423 No article with that number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): ARTICLE -> 220 n message-id Article follows (multi-line)
actions: send 220 response with article number, message-id, and multi-line article body

statements.description: Third form (current article number used): ARTICLE -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): ARTICLE -> 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Indicating capability: READER — the ARTICLE command requires the READER capability to be advertised by the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The server MUST NOT change the currently selected newsgroup as a result of this command.
statements.guard_semantics: MUST NOT change as result of ARTICLE command

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The server MUST NOT change the current article number except when an article number argument was provided and the article exists; in particular, it MUST NOT change it following an unsuccessful response.
statements.guard_semantics: MUST update only when article number argument provided and article exists; MUST NOT change on unsuccessful response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the first form, a message-id is specified, and the server presents the article with that message-id. The server MUST NOT alter the currently selected newsgroup or current article number. The article is returned as a multi-line data block following the 220 response code.
actions: send article headers, empty line, body as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a message-id and no such article exists, a 430 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: ARTICLE <message-id> received, no such article exists

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the second form, an article number is specified. If there is an article with that number in the currently selected newsgroup, the server MUST set the current article number to that number. The article is returned as a multi-line data block following the 220 response code.
statements.trigger: ARTICLE <number> received, article exists in currently selected newsgroup
actions: set current article number to specified number
send article headers, empty line, body as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a number or is omitted and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned. (Form 2: article number argument.)
statements.trigger: ARTICLE <number> received, currently selected newsgroup invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a number and that article does not exist in the currently selected newsgroup, a 423 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: ARTICLE <number> received, article not in currently selected newsgroup

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the third form, the article indicated by the current article number in the currently selected newsgroup is used. The article is returned as a multi-line data block following the 220 response code.
statements.trigger: ARTICLE (no argument) received, valid newsgroup and valid current article number
actions: send article headers, empty line, body as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a number or is omitted and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned. (Form 3: no argument.)
statements.trigger: ARTICLE (no argument) received, currently selected newsgroup invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is omitted and the current article number is invalid, a 420 response MUST be returned.
statements.trigger: ARTICLE (no argument) received, current article number invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD message-id: server responds 221 with headers (multi-line) when article with that message-id exists.
actions: send article headers as multi-line data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD message-id: server responds 430 when no article with that message-id exists.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD number: server responds 221 with headers when a newsgroup is selected and article with that number exists.
actions: send article headers as multi-line data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD number: server responds 412 when no newsgroup is selected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD number: server responds 423 when newsgroup is selected but no article with that number exists.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD (no argument): server responds 221 with headers when newsgroup is selected and current article number is valid.
actions: send article headers as multi-line data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD (no argument): server responds 412 when no newsgroup is selected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HEAD (no argument): server responds 420 when newsgroup is selected but current article number is invalid.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Second and third forms of HEAD require a newsgroup to be selected; absence causes 412 response.
statements.guard_semantics: HEAD number and HEAD (no-arg) forms require session.newsgroup_selected = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Third form of HEAD requires current article number to be valid; absence causes 420 response.
statements.guard_semantics: HEAD (no-arg) form requires session.current_article_number_valid = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The HEAD command behaves identically to the ARTICLE command except that, if the article exists, the response code is 221 instead of 220 and only the headers are presented.
actions: send article headers (no body, no separating empty line)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The empty line separating the headers and body MUST NOT be included in the HEAD response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): BODY message-id -> 222 0|n message-id Body follows (multi-line)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): BODY message-id -> 430 No article with that message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): BODY number -> 222 n message-id Body follows (multi-line)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): BODY number -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): BODY number -> 423 No article with that number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): BODY -> 222 n message-id Body follows (multi-line)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): BODY -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): BODY -> 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Second form (article number specified) requires a newsgroup to be selected; 412 is returned if no newsgroup selected.
statements.guard_semantics: BODY number command requires session.newsgroup_selected = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Third form (current article number used) requires a newsgroup to be selected and the current article number to be valid; 412 if no newsgroup, 420 if current article number is invalid.
statements.guard_semantics: BODY command (no argument) requires session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_number.valid = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The BODY command behaves identically to the ARTICLE command except that, if the article exists, the response code is 222 instead of 220 and only the body is presented (the empty line separating the headers and body MUST NOT be included).
actions: send article body without header-body separator line

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful retrieval of the body of an article (explicitly not using an article number): GROUP misc.test -> 211 1234 3000234 3002322 misc.test; BODY -> 222 3000234 <45223423@example.com> followed by body data.
actions: send 222 response with article-number and message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful retrieval of the body of an article by message-id: BODY <45223423@example.com> -> 222 0 <45223423@example.com> followed by body data.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an unsuccessful retrieval of the body of an article by message-id: BODY <i.am.not.there@example.com> -> 430 No Such Article Found.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an unsuccessful retrieval of the body of an article by number: GROUP misc.test -> 211; BODY 300256 -> 423 No article with that number.
actions: send 423 No article with that number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an unsuccessful retrieval of the body of an article by number because no newsgroup was selected first: [Assumes currently selected newsgroup is invalid.] BODY 300256 -> 412 No newsgroup selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Assumes currently selected newsgroup is invalid — precondition for 412 response to BODY command with article number.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve the body of an article when the currently selected newsgroup is empty: GROUP example.empty.newsgroup -> 211 0 0 0; BODY -> 420 No current article selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Currently selected newsgroup is empty — no current article exists for implicit BODY retrieval, yielding 420.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): STAT message-id -> 223 0|n message-id (Article exists)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First form (message-id specified): STAT message-id -> 430 No article with that message-id

statements.description: Second form (article number specified): STAT number -> 223 n message-id (Article exists)
actions: send 223 response with article number and message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): STAT number -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Second form (article number specified): STAT number -> 423 No article with that number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): STAT -> 223 n message-id (Article exists)
actions: send 223 response with current article number and message-id

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Third form (current article number used): STAT -> 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.description: Third form (current article number used): STAT -> 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 412 No newsgroup selected - second and third forms of STAT require a newsgroup to be selected

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 420 Current article number is invalid - third form of STAT requires a valid current article number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The STAT command behaves identically to the ARTICLE command except that, if the article exists, it is NOT presented to the client and the response code is 223 instead of 220. Note that the response is NOT multi-line.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The STAT command behaves identically to the ARTICLE command except that the response is NOT multi-line; no body transfer state is entered.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of STAT on an article by number when no newsgroup was selected first: [Assumes currently selected newsgroup is invalid.] [C] STAT 300256 [S] 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of STAT on an article when the currently selected newsgroup is empty: [C] STAT [S] 420 No current article selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of STAT on an article not on the server by message-id: [C] STAT <i.am.not.there@example.com> [S] 430 No Such Article Found

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of STAT on an article not in the server by number: [C] STAT 300256 [S] 423 No article with that number
actions: send 423 No article with that number

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of STAT on an existing article (explicitly not using an article number): [C] STAT [S] 223 3000234 <45223423@example.com>

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The last one shows that the current article number is still not changed by the use of STAT with a message-id even if it returns an article number.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The fourth STAT command shows that zero must be specified if the article isn't in the currently selected newsgroup.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The fifth shows that the number, if provided, must be that relating to the currently selected newsgroup.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After server sends 340 (Send article to be posted), the session enters an intermediate state in which the client is expected to transmit the article body before a subsequent response is returned.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client sends POST; server issues initial response 340 (Send article to be posted), transitioning session to the send-article state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client sends POST; server issues initial response 440 (Posting not permitted); no state change (posting rejected).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client transmits article body after 340; server issues subsequent response 240 (Article received OK), concluding the POST transaction.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client transmits article body after 340; server issues subsequent response 441 (Posting failed), concluding the POST transaction with failure.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If posting is allowed, a 340 response MUST be returned to indicate that the article to be posted should be sent.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If posting is prohibited for some installation-dependent reason, a 440 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Following the presentation of the termination sequence by the client, the server MUST return a response indicating success or failure of the article transfer — 240 indicating success.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Following the presentation of the termination sequence by the client, the server MUST return a response indicating success or failure of the article transfer — 441 indicating failure.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If posting is permitted, the article MUST be sent by the client to the server as a multi-line data block. A 340 response indicates that the article to be posted should be sent.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the session is interrupted before the response is received, in any subsequent session, the client SHOULD either check whether the article was successfully posted before resending or ensure that the server will allocate the same message-id to the new attempt.
actions: resend article or ensure same message-id allocation

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends POST; server responds 340 indicating it is ready to receive article input ending with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After article body is submitted (terminated with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>), server responds 240 Article received OK on successful posting.
statements.trigger: article body terminated (end-of-text marker received), posting succeeds

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After article body is submitted (terminated with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>), server responds 441 Posting failed on unsuccessful posting.
statements.trigger: article body terminated (end-of-text marker received), posting fails

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After initial connection set-up completed with 201 (posting prohibited), client sends POST; server responds 440 Posting not permitted and remains in posting-prohibited state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server awaiting article body input after issuing 340; article must be terminated with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After client sends IHAVE message-id, session awaits an initial response (335, 435, or 436) from the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After receiving 335 (Send article to be transferred), session enters a state where the article is being transferred and a subsequent response (235, 436, or 437) is awaited.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client issues IHAVE message-id command; session moves to await initial server response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 335 (Send article to be transferred); client proceeds to send the article body.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 435 (Article not wanted); IHAVE transaction ends without transfer.
actions: IHAVE transaction terminated; article not transferred

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 436 (Transfer not possible; try again later) as initial response; IHAVE transaction ends, client may retry later.
actions: IHAVE transaction terminated; retry permitted later

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 235 (Article transferred OK) after article body sent; IHAVE transaction completes successfully.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 436 (Transfer failed; try again later) as subsequent response; IHAVE transaction ends with failure, retry permitted.
actions: IHAVE transaction terminated; retry permitted later

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Server responds 437 (Transfer rejected; do not retry) as subsequent response; IHAVE transaction ends with permanent rejection.
actions: IHAVE transaction permanently rejected; do not retry

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: IHAVE command MUST NOT be pipelined; each IHAVE exchange must complete before another command is issued.
statements.guard_semantics: IHAVE command must not be sent in a pipeline; sequential execution required

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server desires a copy of that article, a 335 response MUST be returned, instructing the client to send the entire article.
actions: client sends entire article as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not want the article, a 435 response MUST be returned, indicating that the article is not wanted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the article isn't wanted immediately but the client should retry later if possible, a 436 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a 235 response, indicating that the article was successfully transferred.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a 436 response, indicating that the transfer failed but should be tried again later.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = SENDING_ARTICLE & server.transfer_failed = true & server.retry_possible = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a 437 response, indicating that the article was rejected.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A lack of response (such as a dropped network connection or a network timeout) SHOULD be treated the same as a 436 response.
actions: client treats lack of response as 436

statements.subject: session
statements.description: State in which the client has sent IHAVE and is awaiting the server's initial response (335, 435, or 436).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: State in which transmission of the article is in progress, following a 335 response from the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Terminal state after server returns 235, indicating the article was successfully transferred.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Terminal state after server returns 437, indicating the article was rejected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Terminal state after server returns 436 (either during initial response or after article send), indicating retry is needed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends IHAVE <message-id>; server responds 335 Send it; end with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends article body terminated with <CR-LF>.<CR-LF>; server responds 235 Article transferred OK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends article body; server responds 437 Article rejected; don't send again

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends article body; server responds 436 Transfer failed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends IHAVE <message-id> for an article already held; server responds 435 Duplicate

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends IHAVE <message-id>; server requests retry later with 436 Retry later (before article body is sent)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Information commands may be used at any time between the beginning of a session and its termination. Using these commands does not alter any state information.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DATE command: server responds with 111 yyyymmddhhmmss (current UTC date and time). Indicating capability: READER.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HELP command: server responds with 100 (Help text follows, multi-line).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command provides a short summary of the commands that are understood by this implementation of the server. The help text will be presented as a multi-line data block following the 100 response code.
actions: send multi-line data block containing help text

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Indicating capability: READER — the NEWGROUPS command requires the READER capability to be active.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: NEWGROUPS date time [GMT] — Responses: 231 List of new newsgroups follows (multi-line)
actions: send multi-line list of new newsgroups

statements.subject: server
statements.description: NEWNEWS command receives response 230 List of new articles follows (multi-line)
actions: send multi-line list of new articles

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LIST [keyword [wildmat|argument]] command receives response 215 (Information follows, multi-line). If no keyword is provided, it defaults to ACTIVE.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the information is available, it is returned as a multi-line data block following the 215 response code.
statements.trigger: LIST command received, keyword recognised, information available

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the keyword is not recognised, or if an argument is specified and the keyword does not expect one, a 501 response code MUST BE returned.
statements.trigger: LIST command received, keyword not recognised or unexpected argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the keyword is recognised but the server does not maintain the information, a 503 response code MUST BE returned.
statements.trigger: LIST command received, keyword recognised but information not maintained

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The LIST command MUST NOT change the visible state of the server in any way; that is, the behaviour of subsequent commands MUST NOT be affected by whether the LIST command was issued.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: LIST ACTIVE returns a list of valid newsgroups and associated information. If no wildmat is specified, the server MUST include every group that the client is permitted to select with the GROUP command.
actions: send multiline newsgroup list with name, high water mark, low water mark, status per line

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A wildmat MAY be specified, in which case the response is limited to only the groups (if any) whose names match the wildmat.
actions: send multiline newsgroup list filtered by wildmat

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends LIST ACTIVE.TIMES [wildmat]; server responds with 215 information follows and a multi-line list of newsgroup name, creation time, and creator fields, terminated by a single dot.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A wildmat MAY be specified with LIST ACTIVE.TIMES, in which case the response is limited to only the groups (if any) whose names match the wildmat.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends LIST DISTRIB.PATS; server responds with 215 information follows, sends multi-line distrib.pats list, and terminates with a dot.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The information is not newsgroup based, and an argument MUST NOT be specified.
statements.guard_semantics: argument must not be present in LIST DISTRIB.PATS command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client sends LIST NEWSGROUPS; server responds with 215 followed by the newsgroups list (one name and description per line) terminated by a "." on a line by itself.
actions: send newsgroups list lines (name TAB description)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A wildmat MAY be specified with LIST NEWSGROUPS, in which case the response is limited to only the groups (if any) whose names match the wildmat.
actions: send filtered newsgroups list lines matching wildmat

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This keyword MUST be supported by servers advertising the READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER message-id: server responds 224 Overview information follows (multi-line) when article with that message-id exists.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER message-id: server responds 430 No article with that message-id.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER range: server responds 224 Overview information follows (multi-line) when newsgroup is selected and articles exist in range.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER range: server responds 412 No newsgroup selected when no newsgroup is currently selected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER range: server responds 423 No articles in that range when newsgroup is selected but range contains no articles.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER (current article): server responds 224 Overview information follows (multi-line) when newsgroup selected and current article number is valid.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER (current article): server responds 412 No newsgroup selected when no newsgroup is currently selected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: OVER (current article): server responds 420 Current article number is invalid when newsgroup is selected but current article number is invalid.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Second form (range specified) and third form (current article number used) of OVER require that a newsgroup is selected; absence of selected newsgroup yields 412.
statements.guard_semantics: OVER range and OVER (no argument) require protocol.state = Selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the information is available, it is returned as a multi-line data block following the 224 response code.
actions: send multi-line data block with overview fields

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a message-id and no such article exists, a 430 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a range or is omitted and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is a range and no articles in that number range exist in the currently selected newsgroup, including the case where the second number is less than the first one, a 423 response MUST be returned.
statements.pre_cond: command.argument_type = range & session.newsgroup_selected = true & range.articles_exist = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is omitted and the current article number is invalid, a 420 response MUST be returned.
statements.pre_cond: command.argument_type = omitted & session.newsgroup_selected = true & session.current_article_number_valid = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Support for the first (message-id) form is optional. If it is supported, the OVER capability line MUST include the argument MSGID. Otherwise, the capability line MUST NOT include this argument, and the OVER command MUST return the generic response code 503 when this form is used.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it is supported, the OVER capability line MUST include the argument MSGID.
statements.guard_semantics: server.supports_OVER_message_id_form = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an unsuccessful retrieval of overview information by number because no newsgroup was selected first: [Assumes currently selected newsgroup is invalid.] [C] OVER [S] 412 No newsgroup selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an attempt to retrieve information when the currently selected newsgroup is empty: [C] GROUP example.empty.newsgroup [S] 211 0 0 0 example.empty.newsgroup [C] OVER [S] 420 No current article selected

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an unsuccessful retrieval of overview information on an article by number: [C] OVER 300256 [S] 423 No such article in this group

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of an invalid range: [C] OVER 3000444-3000222 [S] 423 Empty range

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of the same commands on a system that does not implement retrieval by message-id: [C] OVER <45223423@example.com> [S] 503 Overview by message-id unsupported

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful retrieval of overview information for an article (explicitly not using an article number): [C] OVER [S] 224 Overview information follows ... [S] .

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful retrieval of overview information for an article by message-id: [C] OVER <45223423@example.com> [S] 224 Overview information follows ... [S] .

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Example of a successful retrieval of overview information for a range of articles: [C] OVER 3000234-3000240 [S] 224 Overview information follows ... [S] .

statements.description: LIST OVERVIEW.FMT command; response 215 Information follows (multi-line)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR field message-id: if article exists, server sends 225 Headers follow (multi-line).

actions: send 430 No article with that message-id

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR field range: if newsgroup selected and articles in range, server sends 225 Headers follow (multi-line).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR field range: if no newsgroup selected, server sends 412.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR field range: if newsgroup selected but no articles in that range, server sends 423.
actions: send 423 No articles in that range

statements.description: HDR field (current article number used): if newsgroup selected and current article valid, server sends 225 Headers follow (multi-line).

statements.description: HDR field (current article number used): if no newsgroup selected, server sends 412.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR field (current article number used): if newsgroup selected but current article number is invalid, server sends 420.
actions: send 420 Current article number is invalid

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR range and current-article forms require a newsgroup to be selected (412 No newsgroup selected).
statements.guard_semantics: HDR range or current-article form requires session.newsgroup_selected = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: HDR current-article form requires a valid current article number (420 Current article number is invalid).

statements.subject: server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the second argument is a message-id and no such article exists, a 430 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY only allow HDR commands for a limited set of fields; if so, it MUST respond with the generic 503 response to attempts to request other fields.

statements.description: If the second argument is a range or is omitted and the currently selected newsgroup is invalid, a 412 response MUST be returned.

statements.guard_semantics: Must be valid (true) for HDR with no argument to succeed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: LIST HEADERS [MSGID|RANGE] — the optional parameter is one of MSGID (requests list for access by message-id) or RANGE (requests list for access by range).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the LIST HEADERS command is received (with optional MSGID or RANGE parameter), the server responds with 215 and sends a multi-line field list.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: While the latest response is one that indicates more data is required (in general, a 3xx response), the client sends an instance of <command-continuation> and the server sends another instance of <response>.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client sends an instance of <command-line>; the server sends an instance of <response>. The initial response line is independent of the command that generated it.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends an instance of <command-line>; the syntax for the EXAMPLE command is <example-command>.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client is one that immediately streams data, it sends an instance of <command-datastream>.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server sends an instance of <response>. If the response is multi-line, the initial line is followed by a <multi-line-data-block>.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: While the latest response is one that indicates more data is required (in general, a 3xx response), the session enters the Continuation Required state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: While the latest response is one that indicates more data is required (in general, a 3xx response), the client sends an instance of <command-continuation>; the server sends another instance of <response>.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: ihave-335-continuation defines the further material sent by the client in the multi-stage IHAVE command after the server has issued a 335 response; the client sends an encoded-article.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: post-340-continuation defines the further material sent by the client in the multi-stage POST command after the server has issued a 340 response; the client sends an encoded-article.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Upon receipt of a 335 response (tentative acceptance of IHAVE), the session enters the ihave-335-continuation stage where the client MUST send an encoded-article (multi-line-data-block).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Upon receipt of a 340 response (send article for POST), the session enters the post-340-continuation stage where the client MUST send an encoded-article (multi-line-data-block).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: encoded-article = multi-line-data-block; after undoing the dot-stuffing, this MUST match <article>. This is the payload required in both ihave-335-continuation and post-340-continuation states.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: what is sent from the server to the client in response to a <command> or a <command-continuation>; response = simple-response / multi-line-response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: initial-response-content = 3DIGIT *(SP response-argument); the three-digit numeric code is mandatory in every response line

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD close the connection if it is no longer possible to parse the NNTP stream sensibly due to malformed or illegal UTF-8 sequences.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Generating a 501 response code in response to detection of malformed or illegal UTF-8 sequences.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD use one of the first two solutions (501 response or replacement character) where the general structure of the NNTP stream remains intact and SHOULD close the connection if it is no longer possible to parse it sensibly.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Initial connection set-up completed; server in initial unencrypted ready state, responding with 200 NNTP Service Ready.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: After client and server negotiate encryption on the link and server responds 283 Encrypted link established, the connection is in the encrypted link state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client sends XENCRYPT; client and server negotiate encryption on the link; server responds 283 Encrypted link established, transitioning the connection to the encrypted state.
actions: capability list updated to reflect encrypted-state extensions

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client sends XSECRET on an encrypted link; server responds 290 Password accepted.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client sends XSECRET on an unencrypted link; server responds 483 Only permitted on secure links; connection state does not change.
actions: server sends 483 Only permitted on secure links

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Whenever there is a relevant change to the server state, the results of the CAPABILITIES command are required to change accordingly.
statements.guard_semantics: capability list must reflect current server state
